title: POV: You become a top caller on Pump.fun

scenes.narration: Congratulations. You're a top caller. For now. Fiction, not financial advice.

True story. Pump.fun has paid callers since August 2026. [src:pumpfun-callout-rewards-program] By November, one research firm estimated the median reward recipient's total at {$13|thirteen dollars}... [src:pumpfun-callout-rewards-concentration] Thirteen.
A friend offers to help. Hypothetically. You call a made-up coin. Your followers pile in. The price spikes, then collapses as other wallets sell. Your followers are left holding it.

An investigator maps your wallets. Your public wallet lost money. The side wallets bought seconds earlier, sold first, and didn't lose. A map cannot say whose they are... You can. Followers leave. Rewards stop. Congratulations.

onScreen.title: The map
bullets: Side wallets: sold first and showed a gain

scenes.narration: Real life. {Bubblemaps|Bubble maps} alleged a similar side-wallet pattern, in what it calls analysis and estimates. [src:bubblemaps-side-wallet-pattern,bubblemaps-analysis-and-estimates]

onScreen.title: Outside the story
bullets: Alleged, not proven; ownership not established

sources.title: crypto.news on Callout Rewards, Nov 2026
sources.quote: … in August, around the time Pump.fun introduced its Callout Rewards program … Under the platform's Callout Rewards terms, last updated on Aug. 13, eligible participants can receive USDC payments based on engagement and trading activity associated with their recommendations.

sources.title: crypto.news on Sparsity Research, Nov 2026
sources.quote: According to a Nov. 10 report from Sparsity Research, approximately 51,115 wallets had received a combined $29.6 million in callout rewards since August. … Ten wallets collected roughly 16% of the total distributed, while the median recipient earned just $13.

sources.title: crypto.news on Bubblemaps, Nov 7, 2026
sources.quote: Bubblemaps has accused crypto influencers of using hidden wallets to profit from their followers … Its account described a public-wallet purchase accompanied by purchases from three alleged side wallets, followed by a recommendation and subsequent selling.
